title: Pete Buttigieg Hiring Goldman Sachs Bankers
description: Don't miss your chance to win a trip to Los Angeles and dinner with the TYT hosts at https://www.TYT.com/dinnerinLA   Pete Buttigieg is filling his campaign with corruption. Ana Kasparian and John Iadarola, hosts of The Young Turks, break it down. TEll us what you think in the comments below.  MORE TYT: https://tyt.com/trial  Read more here:  https://www.cnbc.com/2019/07/18/buttigieg-hires-former-goldman-sachs-executive-as-policy-director.html  "Democratic presidential contender Pete Buttigieg has hired a former Goldman Sachs vice president and Google executive to run his policy shop, his campaign announced Thursday.  Sonal Shah, now executive director of the Beeck Center for Social Impact and Innovation at Georgetown University, will be the campaign’s national policy director.  Shah worked at Goldman Sachs from 2004 to 2007 as a vice president, according to her LinkedIn page. She then worked for Google as its head of global development initiatives from 2007 to 2009.  The hiring comes as Buttigieg, mayor of South Bend, Indiana, struggles to stake out a clear niche for himself in a crowded Democratic field featuring a number of high-profile progressives." asr.full_text: We have more news on Pete Buttigieg today that I can't wait to share with you. Pete Buttigieg has decided to completely move away from his so called, progressive label, and that makes a lot of sense because clearly he's not a progressive. And he does have a lot of affection for the financial industry and especially Goldman Sachs. One piece of evidence for that is that he just hired a former Goldman Sachs executive as his national policy director. Now, this got pretty good coverage at CNBC, but I'm not seeing it reported anywhere else to be honest, but- CNBC highly critical, I assume? Actually, to be fair, CNBC did a good job with this story. They fact check the Buttigieg campaign, and so credit where credit is due. In terms of what that person has actually done in their past. Exactly. Yes, okay, that's true. So let's get to those details. So who is this person who's gonna be in charge of advising his campaign on national policy? Well, her name is Sonal Shah and she worked at Goldman Sachs from 2004 to 2007, those years are pretty relevant, as a vice president, that's according to our LinkedIn page. Now she then worked for Google as its head of global development initiatives from 2007 to 2009. So she's had some pretty big roles in many of the corporations that have had problematic histories, in some cases. So she developed and managed Goldman Sachs is environmental strategy according to Chris Meagher who's Buttigieg's as campaign press secretary. She trained bankers to ask environmental questions, manage the grants to nonprofits, and worked with their real estate team on how to build more green buildings. That sounds good. That sounds pretty good, right? Like I mean we like environmental stuff, right? Yeah, and green infrastructure that sounds good. Well, CNBC did a little bit of fact checking. In contribution records filed with the Federal Election Commission from the period, Shaw listed her occupation at varying times as investment banker, economist, and vice-president. Investment banker is a little bit different from some environmental activist within the corporation, just putting that out there. Now in early 2017, Shah also cheered president trump's decision to hire a former Goldman Saxe executive by the name of Dina Powell. And so she is, well, let's look at the tweet first, great choice, Deena Powell will be great. Trump hires another executive from Goldman Sachs, okay? So she was hired as Deputy National Security Advisor. So Buttigieg's campaign also claimed that Shaw worked at the Obama White House after the financial crisis. She doesn't advocate for companies. She cares about having the greatest social impact for people. And finding new solutions to tough challenges that require the public, and private, and social sectors to work together to find them. That's why she's teaching at Georgetown after leaving the White House. So, wow, that's big. You walk away from the White House. It's a pretty incredible job. Lots of prestige there and you decide. I just wanna be a professor, really want to connect with the students. But at Georgetown, Shaw was a professor and the founder of the peak Center for Social Impact and Innovation. The center was founded with a 10 million dollar donation from investor Alberto Beek a former Lehman Brothers investment banker who is now focused on mining hotels wealth management telecom and tech sectors hmm which ones the green one lots of philanthropic work going on there yeah yeah look and I'm sure if you go back to your past, there's some good stuff or whatever. But it seems like they're presenting an image of her past that isn't necessarily supported by a lot of evidence. And even if it was, I think that this hire, it shows what they're worried about and what they're not worried about in the Buttigieg campaign. Because for Buttigieg to have a path going forward, he could either try to maybe reassert his former, like he made some comments, are very supportive of Medicare for all, like a billion years ago. It's two, but he's changed law since then. Yes. He could do that. But you don't do that if you're hiring Goldman Sachs people. You understand full well what message that's gonna send to people. And so, if you're doing that, it gives us a pretty clear signal about which path he is going to try to go for it. It is very much the one that Biden is receding from right now. You can and indeed should hire people from Goldman Sachs. If your fundraising strategy is gonna be incredibly reliant on rich donors and from Wall Street specifically. If you're doing that, then you're not worried at all about the appearance that you're hiring people who theoretically might have been around that whole thing right before the economy collapse. Right, I think that's a great point. It's what a former Goldman Sachs' VP represents, at a time when wealth and income inequality is at an incredible, you see this disparity between the rich and the poor in America and that gap continues to widen. People are very much concerned about the inequality and how you can redistribute the wealth in the richest country in the world. And Pete Buttigieg is, yeah, the progressive thing, it didn't come across as authentic because no one's buying it. So this Biden guy not doing so well, maybe I can go ahead and appeal to some of his voters. So he's made a political calculation here, but it's important to keep in mind that on one hand you have a candidate who has been consistent in fighting for the same issues, the working class, his entire political career. And then on the other hand you have Peabodyge a 37 year old who's inexperienced, who was a failure as mayor of South Bend. The racial tensions in that county became much worse under his leadership, or lack of leadership. And to see him just kind of have just have this fluid political identity depending on what's convenient for him in that moment speaks a lot of who he is and what he represents.
